name: PySceneDetect
role: Shot boundary detection CLI and Python library over OpenCV; splits video via FFmpeg
summary: Python CLI and library that finds scene cuts in video using content, adaptive, threshold and histogram detectors on OpenCV frames, and outputs timecode lists, CSV, thumbnails, or split clips by calling FFmpeg or mkvmerge. Distinguishing strength: ready-made cut detection with tunable detectors, so an agent need not write frame-diff code.
use_when: Splitting footage into shots or listing cut timecodes, over a hand-rolled FFmpeg scene filter
Producing an edit decision list from source footage for VCR's timeline
Generating one thumbnail per shot for a contact sheet
avoid_when: Only a rough scene score is needed: ffmpeg select='gt(scene,0.4)' needs no Python
Semantic scene understanding: PySceneDetect finds visual cuts, not meaning
notes: 2026-10-26: Python 3.10+ required; the scenedetect[opencv] extra pulls a large OpenCV wheel.

assessment.rationale: Version 0.7.2 on PyPI released 2026-10-12, BSD-3-Clause, requires Python 3.10+. Active and unique among our tools for shot detection; FFmpeg's scene filter is the lightweight alternative.
